quests.title: Caravan Escort Mission
quests.description: A trading caravan requests an armed escort through dangerous territory.
quests.synopsis: The Black Flotilla's trading caravan is traveling through Sector 6, a known raider territory. They offer payment in exchange for armed escort.

choices.consequences: The caravan reaches its destination safely, and you receive payment. However, the raiders may seek revenge.
The caravan is ambushed, and the Black Flotilla blames you for the loss. Your reputation suffers.

choices.text: Ambush the caravan and steal their goods
choices.consequences: The caravan is robbed, but the Black Flotilla vows revenge. Raiders may now target your bunker.

quests.title: Experimental Drug Trial
quests.description: Dr. Vasquez proposes testing an experimental drug on a terminally ill survivor.
quests.synopsis: Dr. Elena Vasquez has developed an experimental drug that could cure radiation sickness. She proposes testing it on Marcus Olejnik, who is terminally ill.

choices.consequences: The drug works! Marcus recovers, and Dr. Vasquez gains prestige. However, the drug has unknown long-term side effects.
Marcus dies, and Dr. Vasquez is devastated. Survivors question the ethics of refusing to try new treatments.

choices.text: Force Marcus to take the drug
choices.consequences: Marcus recovers, but survivors are horrified by the forced treatment. Trust in leadership erodes.

quests.title: Survivor Exile Decision
quests.description: A survivor has broken a critical rule and must be exiled for the safety of the group.
quests.synopsis: Jamie has been stealing food from the bunker's storage. The survivors must decide whether to exile them or give them a second chance.

choices.consequences: Jamie is exiled, but survivors are divided. Some may leave in protest, while others feel justice has been served.

choices.text: Forgive Jamie and assign community service
choices.consequences: Jamie is forgiven and assigned community service. Survivors respect the decision, and morale improves.
The theft continues, and survivors grow resentful. Some may start stealing for themselves.

quests.title: Radiation Storm Shelter Plan
quests.description: Prepare the bunker for an impending radiation storm.
quests.synopsis: Meteorologists predict a severe radiation storm in 72 hours. The bunker must prepare by sealing the air filters, stocking supplies, and assigning shelter duties.

choices.consequences: The bunker survives the storm with minimal casualties. Survivors are relieved and grateful.
The bunker suffers some radiation exposure, but no one is critically injured. Survivors are uneasy about the bunker's readiness.
The storm hits, and survivors suffer radiation exposure. Some may not survive.

quests.title: Command Structure Audit
quests.description: Personnel are organizing to formally challenge the current command hierarchy.
quests.synopsis: A coalition of units has demanded a formalized transition of command, citing recent caloric deficits. They are attempting to institute an electoral protocol to replace your authority.

choices.consequences: You step down. The coalition installs a new director. Your personal caloric allocation is immediately reduced to baseline.
You refuse to acknowledge the protocol. The coalition attempts a labor strike, which you break by withholding rations. Efficiency remains crippled for weeks.
You rig the ballot collection. You retain command, but the obvious manipulation permanently damages the settlement's operational cohesion.

quests.title: Caloric Storage Optimization
quests.description: The current organization of the cold-stores is resulting in unacceptable spoilage rates.
quests.synopsis: Improper stacking and poor air circulation in the food reserves are causing baseline rations to rot before consumption. Reorganizing the space requires halting all other labor for two shifts.

choices.consequences: You divert the labor. The reorganization stops the spoilage, securing the winter supply, though the lost operational time delays structural repairs.
You re-stack only the most perishable items. The spoilage rate is halved, but remains a constant drain on the ledger.
Labor continues on schedule. The spoilage continues unchecked, forcing severe rationing later in the season.

quests.title: Cross-Disciplinary Labor Initiative
quests.description: A proposal to cross-train units to reduce single-point-of-failure vulnerabilities.
quests.synopsis: The settlement relies heavily on isolated specialists. A proposal has been filed to cross-train standard labor units in mechanical and agricultural maintenance.

choices.consequences: You divert operational time to the training. General efficiency drops temporarily, but the settlement becomes highly resilient to targeted casualties.
You train backups only for the water cycler and generator. The vulnerability is reduced, but the agricultural sector remains exposed.
You maximize immediate output. A subsequent accident claims the primary botanist, and hydroponic yields plummet.

quests.title: Sector Blockade
quests.description: A hostile faction has established a perimeter blockade, cutting off scavenging routes.
quests.synopsis: Armed hostiles have surrounded the primary exits. They are demanding a transfer of medical supplies and ammunition to lift the blockade. Refusal guarantees a breach attempt.

choices.consequences: You man the barricades. The hostiles attempt a breach and are repelled, but you expend 40% of your ammunition reserves in the process.
You pay the toll. The hostiles withdraw. Your reserves are severely depleted, but the physical structure and personnel remain intact.
You open the gates. The hostiles strip the settlement of all high-value assets and relegate your personnel to forced labor.

quests.title: Biological Contagion Protocol
quests.description: A unit is displaying symptoms of an unidentified, highly communicable pathogen.
quests.synopsis: Unit Alex-9 is exhibiting acute respiratory distress and elevated temperature. The pathogen's transmission vector is unknown, but standard modeling suggests high virulency.

choices.consequences: You isolate the unit in a sealed sector. The pathogen does not spread. The unit's labor is lost for the duration of the quarantine.
You keep the unit on shift. The pathogen spreads rapidly. Production halts entirely as 30% of the settlement becomes symptomatic.
You force the unit out of the airlock. The contagion risk is eliminated instantly, though the permanent loss of the asset impacts long-term projections.

quests.title: Neurological Degradation
quests.description: An asset is experiencing severe cognitive decline, compromising operational efficiency.
quests.synopsis: Unit Jamie-2 has begun failing to execute basic procedural tasks and cannot recall recent directives. The degradation appears neurological and irreversible.

choices.consequences: You assign the unit to basic hauling tasks. They require constant supervision, creating a net drag on efficiency, but continue to provide raw muscle.
You deem the unit a liability and expel them. The settlement's overall efficiency stabilizes, though the raw labor pool decreases.
You ignore the issue. The unit eventually causes a critical failure in the water filtration system due to a forgotten maintenance step.

quests.title: Atmospheric Filtration Overhaul
quests.description: The primary air scrubbers require a massive overhaul to maintain safe particulate levels.
quests.synopsis: The carbon filters in the main ventilation shaft are fully saturated. Replacing them requires cannibalizing scarce activated charcoal and halting air circulation for twelve hours.

choices.consequences: The new filters are installed. Ambient radiation drops to zero. The 12-hour air stoppage causes minor hypoxia in several units.
You replace only the intake filter. The air quality improves marginally, but long-term respiratory issues remain statistically probable.
You conserve the charcoal. The filters fail completely two weeks later, requiring an emergency evacuation of the lower levels.

quests.title: Non-Essential Data Archival
quests.description: Personnel are requesting resources to document pre-war cultural data.
quests.synopsis: A coalition of units has requested paper, pigments, and operational downtime to record subjective memories of the pre-war era. This activity yields zero caloric or defensive value.

choices.consequences: You provide the materials. The units complete the archival project. General efficiency increases slightly, though the consumed resources cannot be recovered.
You refuse the request. The materials are conserved for utilitarian purposes. A minor, persistent drop in operational focus is logged across the involved units.
You attempt to systematize the project, demanding rigid documentation. The units lose interest. The effort wastes time and produces unusable data.

quests.title: Meridian Compact Data Exchange
quests.description: The Meridian Compact offers pre-war schematics in exchange for material resources.
quests.synopsis: A Meridian envoy has presented a verifiable schematic for a high-efficiency water condenser. They demand a significant transfer of medical supplies and preserved food to release the data.

choices.consequences: You transfer the supplies. The schematic is valid, and the new condenser permanently resolves your localized water deficit.
You refuse to part with the medical supplies. The envoy departs. You retain your immediate medical capacity, but the water deficit remains critical.
You attempt to copy the schematic during the negotiation without payment. The envoy detects the breach, seals the data, and blacklists your settlement.
